messages:
ashley: heads-up — after the 2.3.0 rollout we saw exporter CPU spike ~2x on the telemetry side. p99 tail for ingestion path climbed to ~480ms for a short window. wondering if span volume or batching changed

deploy-bot: deploy/2.3.0 finished rolling to prod at 2025-03-12T15:22:17Z :rocket:

mohit: do we have a diff of emitted spans per-second vs pre-rollout? could be extra instrumentation firing on hot paths

ashley: I grabbed a quick metric dump: `otel_spans_emitted_total` doubled for the inference service between 15:20-15:28. exporter queue length peaked at 12k, exporter CPU went from 18% -> 42% on the host pool

lina: can you paste the exporter logs? curious if we're seeing repeated retries or serialization latency

ashley: log snippet below (truncated):
```
2025-03-12T15:24:02Z ERROR exporter_client.go:142 send failed: timeout
2025-03-12T15:24:03Z WARN  exporter_queue.go:78 queue_len=12034 drops=124
2025-03-12T15:24:04Z INFO  batch_processor.go:56 batch_size=8 avg_process_ns=420000
```

samir: interesting that avg_process_ns is 420k (420µs) per batch — shouldn't tank CPU that much unless batch count is huge. if spans are tiny, overhead is per-request serialization + http client churn

mohit: any sampling config changes in 2.3.0? or we accidentally enabled detailed db spans for the hot path?

ashley: no explicit sampling flips. but there was a change in the app instrumentation: we switched a couple of middleware spans from `span.end()` at request end to ending per internal op — might have multiplied span count for common requests

lina: sounds like a good candidate for span-merge on hot paths (coalesce short internal spans into one summarized span). that would reduce span_count and amortize exporter serialization. propose temporary service-side merge + adaptive batching

mohit: also possible to tune exporter batching params: increase `max_queue_size`, bump `max_export_batch_size` to 128, and raise `schedule_delay_millis` from 500 -> 750ms. that will raise tail latency but reduce CPU/time-to-send tradeoff. we should simulate

samir: can we do a quick local repro? emulate request QPS and the new instrumentation to see CPU and p99 after different batch configs. I can spin up a harness today

ashley: yes please. also open question: retention/ingest side — the collector was dropping spans when queue > 10k which caused retries. retries might explain CPU thrash on exporter side too. collector logs show `backpressure=true` around same time

lina: action items:
- samir: run local harness with new instrumentation and try batch sizes [32,64,128] and schedule_delay [250,500,750]
- mohit: prototype a lightweight span-merge heuristic: merge consecutive subspans < 3ms under same parent if they are >10 per request
- ashley: add a short-term rollout to reduce instrumentation detail for inference hot path and monitor emitter metrics

mohit: one more note — we should avoid permanent dropping; instead prefer summarized spans to preserve signal for downstream metrics and audits

ashley: agreed. I'll file an incident note and tag support. we'll treat this as low-sev for now since SLA unaffected but risky for long tail

deploy-bot: incident-1234 created by ashley: "Telemetry exporter CPU spike after 2.3.0 — investigating span volume and batching"

samir: starting harness now, will post results in this thread within 2 hours :eyes:

lina: thanks — keeping this thread for config proposals and numbers. if anyone has quick scripts for generating synthetic spans, ping me.

ashley: thanks team :thumbsup:
